authority_contract.loading_rule: Only entries with authoritative=true and kit_treatment=authoritative-extracted-beta may be loaded or presented as DDD rule authority.
authority_contract.standards_boundary: Standards support records an outcome-level alignment only. It does not establish field usefulness, implementation correctness, runtime capability, project applicability, portability evidence, extraction readiness, or conformance.
authority_contract.profile_adapter_boundary: Profiles and adapters may bind company, project, domain, repository, tool, runtime, threshold, and ownership details. They must not weaken a triggered core invariant, change upstream portability status, or present local policy as universal authority.

The current complexity and coupling sensor policy is project-local.

rules.trigger: Before architecture or solution commitment when a requested outcome, current operational reality, and proposed solution have not been separated.
rules.applicability: Material Discovery or Design work whose solution choice could constrain the problem definition.
rules.invariant: Record the requested outcome and demonstrated operational reality independently from any proposed solution before selecting architecture.
rules.expected_outcome: Unsupported solution classes can be rejected without losing the underlying need, and solution-first assumptions do not become accepted problem framing.
rules.authority_boundary: The evidence owner records current reality; the named human decision owner approves product value, priority, and acceptable error cost.
rules.stop_or_narrow: If outcome or current reality is unsupported, keep it provisional or unknown and stop architecture selection at the affected boundary.
limitations: The evidence does not isolate a universal time saving.

rules.trigger: When a material claim will be used to frame, select, authorize, validate, or close work.
rules.applicability: Claims whose evidentiary state can change a material decision.
rules.invariant: Record each material claim as confirmed, provisional, unknown, or rejected from current evidence. The state records evidence sufficiency only; it does not grant decision authority, and absent evidence remains unknown rather than becoming a default.
rules.expected_outcome: Missing evidence and produced output cannot silently become facts, defaults, or decision authority.
rules.authority_boundary: The evidence owner classifies the claim; the separately named decision owner decides within their authority after required validation.
rules.stop_or_narrow: If a required state cannot be supported, mark it unknown and narrow or stop the dependent decision.
limitations: No expanded basis or lifecycle taxonomy is part of the generic rule.
Per-rule labeling cost was not measured consistently across contexts.
non_goals: Defining project-specific evidence labels or sources
Using evidence state as approval or authority

rules.trigger: When deterministic processing, AI proposals, validation, material decisions, or side effects contribute to one workflow or change.
rules.applicability: Material Design work with more than one type of evidence producer, validator, decision maker, or side-effect owner.
rules.invariant: Assign deterministic processing, AI proposals, validation, material decisions, and side effects to explicit owners. Ownership identifies responsibility and decision authority; it does not validate content. AI output remains untrusted until the required deterministic validation or named human judgment accepts it.
rules.expected_outcome: Evidence producers cannot self-authorize material decisions, and an ownership map cannot be mistaken for proof that AI content is correct.
rules.authority_boundary: Validators own their declared evidence gates; named human owners retain material judgment and risk acceptance; side-effect owners enforce the approved outcome.
rules.stop_or_narrow: If validation or decision authority is missing or unavailable, stop or narrow the dependent action.
limitations: Ownership did not eliminate false semantic or authority claims in the reviewed contexts.
Project roles, identities, risk values, and enforcement mechanisms remain target-specific.

rules.trigger: At a material transition between outcome framing, design selection, Delivery, evaluation, adoption, promotion, or later work.
rules.applicability: Material work where evidence or completion in one stage could be mistaken for authority to enter another.
rules.invariant: Track outcome agreement, design selection, and Delivery authorization independently; no state, evidence result, recommendation, or elapsed time implies another state.
rules.expected_outcome: Accepted evidence or completed work cannot silently authorize a later stage, product continuation, or portability promotion.
rules.authority_boundary: Only the named human decision owner may select, authorize, revoke, adopt, or promote within the authority assigned to that transition.
rules.stop_or_narrow: If the exact next-stage authority is absent, keep that stage locked while allowing already authorized evidence work to close within its boundary.
limitations: No common per-transition timing or false-positive stop rate was established.
Role names and approval systems remain target-specific.
non_goals: Turning feasibility or evaluation success into authorization

rules.trigger: Before Delivery begins for material work and when that work is reviewed against its authorized boundary.
rules.applicability: Material work that changes ownership, interface, dependency, persistence, failure, deployment, contract, or internal-complexity boundaries. A mechanical leaf exception is permitted only when none changes materially.
rules.invariant: Keep a durable authoritative design record containing the selected boundary, independent approval states, acceptance gates, unchanged contracts, and stop conditions; review resolves that record and checks the authorized phase against the change.
rules.expected_outcome: Design, authority, and evidence remain reconstructable outside chat, and review can reject work outside the selected and authorized phase.
rules.authority_boundary: The named human owner selects and authorizes material work; the reviewer verifies record-to-change alignment and any claimed leaf exception.
rules.stop_or_narrow: Missing authority, a missing durable record for material work, or an unsupported leaf exception keeps Delivery locked.
limitations: Small-leaf false-positive rates and per-rule elapsed cost remain unmeasured.
Artifact format, repository location, and approval system remain target-specific.
non_goals: Requiring a new plan for every mechanical leaf change
Making chat an authoritative design store

rules.trigger: When an isolated adapter, spike, prototype, experiment, or other enabling slice is proposed or completed for a parent outcome.
rules.applicability: Enabling work whose success could otherwise be mistaken for parent design, integration, product, or next-stage approval.
rules.invariant: An enabling slice proves only its predeclared bounded feasibility claim; parent design selection and integration or Delivery authorization remain separate and locked.
rules.expected_outcome: A successful mechanism cannot inherit or manufacture authority for its parent outcome.
rules.authority_boundary: The enabling-slice owner closes the bounded evidence claim; the named parent decision owner separately selects and authorizes parent work.
rules.stop_or_narrow: Close the enabling work at its evidence boundary and keep the parent locked when parent selection or authorization is absent.
limitations: The rule requires a compact claim and parent-boundary record.
Prospective correction and false-positive counts remain open in two contexts.
non_goals: Authorizing parent integration from feasibility success

rules.source_rule_summary: Establish current source, artifact, and relevant installed-trial provenance before relying on a packaged or deployed trial.
rules.missing_gate: Track stale identity and configuration detections, avoided retries, false positives, overhead, and applicability in a materially different packaged or deployed system before source-owned promotion review.

standards_support.outcome: Prove current source, build, and artifact identity before relying on an installed trial.
standards_support.limitations: Build provenance alone does not prove installed activation, effective configuration, live capability, client files, service identities, or host-specific preflight.

supporting_contexts: KCS stateful model/tool continuation corrections
API engineering toolkit retry and concurrency applicability review
rules.trigger: When duplicate, re-entrant, retried, or rejected submission could repeat a side effect or corrupt the identity or lifecycle of a logical operation.
rules.applicability: Stateful or side-effecting continuations with a material duplicate-safety risk. Stateless or side-effect-free paths need no retry mechanism when the applicability review records that the invariant cannot be violated.
rules.invariant: One logical action produces at most one side effect; an exact duplicate receives the same stable outcome or a deterministic no-op; a conflicting or stale submission cannot alter or consume a different current operation; and a rejected submission that changed no state preserves any still-valid operation unless an identity or lifecycle conflict is established.
rules.expected_outcome: Retries and duplicates cannot repeat side effects, destroy valid pending work, or let stale submissions interfere with unrelated current work.
rules.authority_boundary: The deterministic owner normalizes equivalent accepted inputs and owns the target-appropriate mechanism and any retention bounds; a model, prompt, or transport cannot supply enforcement by instruction.
rules.stop_or_narrow: Do not rely on the path operationally until applicable duplicate, conflict, stale, and rejected-submission outcomes are tested; otherwise restrict or narrow the supported operation.
limitations: The external use was retrospective and did not execute one prospective runtime retry/concurrency path.
No target API, operation-identity, retention, cache, persistence, or transport mechanism is required by the generic rule.
non_goals: Mandating a storage or replay mechanism
Requiring retry controls for paths where the invariant cannot be violated

supporting_contexts: KCS mixed and uncommitted installed-evidence incident
API engineering toolkit lost evidence packet and later commit-backed adoption
rules.trigger: Before declaring material version-controlled work delivered or using it to authorize later material work.
rules.applicability: Material repository work with validation or built/installed evidence that must be attributable to an exact intended change.
rules.invariant: Isolate the intended change from unrelated or deferred work, review and validate that isolated state, record a durable revision or an explicitly approved no-revision/defer disposition, and keep accepted artifact evidence traceable to the durable content. Mixed or provisional evidence cannot authorize the next material stage.
rules.expected_outcome: Delivered content and its evidence are reconstructable, reviewable, and not confused with unrelated or provisional work.
rules.authority_boundary: The change owner isolates and validates the work; the named human owner approves any no-revision/defer disposition and later-stage authorization.
rules.stop_or_narrow: Keep delivery and the next material stage open when the intended change is mixed, unreviewed, not durably identified without approval, or artifact evidence is not traceable.
limitations: One original external evidence packet remains permanently lost.
Exact per-rule timing and approved no-revision false positives are unknown.
non_goals: Forbidding an explicitly approved no-revision or defer path

supporting_contexts: KCS synthetic-to-representative outcome correction
standalone engineering investigation hidden representative gates
scientific feasibility physical-case contract
rules.trigger: Before closing work with a claim about a named incident, noisy input, deployment failure, or parent operational outcome.
rules.applicability: Completion claims whose truth depends on more than the mechanism, contract, wiring, or bounded feasibility already tested.
rules.invariant: Map the claim to the smallest safe evidence level capable of proving it. Fixtures and synthetic smokes may prove contracts, mechanics, safety, wiring, or feasibility. Representative or real operational evidence is required only when the completion claim depends on that level; it is not a default for every change.
rules.expected_outcome: Weaker synthetic evidence cannot close a stronger operational claim, while low-risk work is not burdened with an unnecessary production trial.
rules.authority_boundary: The evidence owner classifies what each result proves; the named human decision owner approves the completion claim and required risk level.
rules.stop_or_narrow: If the required evidence is unavailable, unsafe, deferred, or fails, narrow the completion claim and keep the stronger outcome open.
limitations: Representative evidence can be materially expensive or unavailable.
The rule makes no claim that every slice needs a real-production trial.
non_goals: Using a fixture to prove an operational outcome it does not exercise
